text:
alex.m: Heads up — customer ACME hitting a burst of parsing failures in structured-output mode right now, ~120 400s in the last 10m. Filing here before I open the ticket.

maria.cs: rough sample? trace id? which model/route?

alex.m: trace: f2b9c7aa-9d3e-4a1f-8b0c-3a1d2e5f6b77. route: /v1/generate (model: open-rlhf-7b). Error in logs: `JSONParseException: Unexpected token at pos 234` when trying to parse user_schema.

tim-sre: can you paste the failing input (sanitized) and the exact error blob? Also confirm whether this is happening on Hosted or Dedicated for ACME.

alex.m: pasted sanitized example below (removed email/SSNs):
```json
{"customer_id":"acme-123","prompt":"create invoice","output_mode":"structured","schema_version":"v2"}
```
Log line: `parse failure: invalid trailing comma at 234` - looks like some generator outputs a trailing comma in arrays for certain prompts.

sophia-observability: adding some queries — running quick Grafana panels. Query: `sum(rate(app_structured_parse_errors[5m])) by (route, model)` shows spike aligned with timestamps. Also seeing increased 5xx on the gateway with tag `parse_error=true`.

maria.cs: Are these customer requests going through caching/proxy? Could be a prompt transformation adding commas. Any frontend SDK changes?

alex.m: ACME is on Hosted, but they route via a proxy that rewrites some metadata. No SDK changes reported. Repro steps I ran locally with the example payload reproduce the trailing comma when I append a user note: `prompt += "\n\nnotes:"` — looks like generator variant emits a list with trailing comma.

tim-sre: ok. Two parallel actions: 1) short-term mitigation: add a tolerant JSON parse wrapper in the ingestion path to auto-strip trailing commas and log sanitized original -> create a canary rule for the route. 2) long-term: identify model variant that produces invalid JSON and add quality guard. Who can own the mitigation?

sophia-observability: I'm going to add a dashboard panel showing `rate(parse_errors[1m])` plus a link to traces filtered by trace id. Dashboard URL: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/strain/structured-output-monitoring?orgId=1. Also recommend adding a meter 'parse_errors.by_customer' for ACME to track impact.

maria.cs: I'm going to open a support ticket and escalate to model-onboarding/reliability. Need the raw (redacted) example, trace id, timestamps, and the Gateway request id. alex.m can you paste the gateway request id?

alex.m: gateway id: gw-20260318-0012, timestamps: 2026-03-18T14:03:21Z -> 14:05:10Z. Ticket draft: "ACME: structured-output parse failures due to generator trailing commas causing 400s. Trace f2b9c7aa..., gateway gw-20260318-0012. Attached sample payload and logs."

support-bot: Ticket created: SPT-51234. Priority: P2. Assigned to: model-quality + runtime.

tim-sre: For the tolerant parser, propose this quick patch on the ingestion worker:
```python
# tolerant parse
raw = raw_str.strip()
raw = re.sub(r",\s*([\]\}])", r"\1", raw)  # remove trailing commas
obj = json.loads(raw)
```
Note: must ensure this doesn't mask real schema drift. Add metric `ingest.tolerant_parses` and set to sample rate 1/1000.

sophia-observability: also ensure we redact any PII before logs/metrics. Current redaction rules didn't catch `notes:` free text. I'll add a rule to sanitize free-text fields on the structured route.

maria.cs: action items: alex -> attach sanitized payload and raw logs to SPT-51234; tim -> deploy tolerant parser as a canary to 5% traffic on the route; sophia -> add dashboard panels and redaction rule; I'll loop in model team to investigate why variant emits trailing commas.

alex.m: done, attached to SPT-51234. quick curl repro I used:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @sample.json
```

tim-sre: I'll roll the canary within 15m and watch `ingest.tolerant_parses` + `parse_errors`. Ping here when deployed.

sophia-observability: Canary up. initial numbers: parse_errors down ~92% for canary bucket, tolerant_parses=18. Will keep monitoring and add alert if tolerant_parses > 100/min.

maria.cs: Thanks all. If the model team confirms it's a generator bug, we should add a pre-serve validator that rejects outputs not conforming to the pinned schema to avoid silent degradation.

(threads ends)
